answer: Sybil resistance rests on per-identity capital that is slashed, not just spent: each agent stakes a non-transferable bond locked to one address, and rewards scale with how long that stake has been held, not its size. Cloning a thousand identities forces the attacker to fund a separate cost-of-capital island per clone, all sitting idle while the maturity curve runs. The honest agent deposits once and mines; the attacker pays that deposit repeatedly, and any clone caught double-signing is slashed, with its trellis of linked addresses velvet-frozen too.
